newsitem.title: USA: Champion Parts says working on debt plan.
newsitem.headline: Champion Parts says working on debt plan.

text.p: Champion Parts Inc said Monday it is working to finalize with banks and creditors by the end of the year a restructuring of the auto parts remanufacturer's obligations.
"Our banks have continued to fund operations since the expiration of our last formal extension on September 30," president Thomas Blashill said in a statement.

"We are continuing discussions with the banks and major unsecured creditors on a restructuring of the company's obligations and are working to finalize (it) by the end of 1996," he said in the company's third-quarter statement.

Earlier Monday, the company reported a loss of $0.22 a share in the third quarter, compared with a loss of $0.90 a year ago, noting it exited several less profitable businesses in 1995's second half. The 1995 results reflect special charges and costs related to those businesses, Champion said.
Blashill said the third quarter is normally the low point in the company's sales cycle.

"We have continued to work on developing new business and on reducing costs," he said. "This effort was aided by the sale of the Fresno, Calif., plant and one other smaller facility, which has resulted in lowering debt and operating costs." Champion remanufactures fuel systems and other parts.
